answer.summary: Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, we calculated the sample size required to estimate a proportion of 0.70 with a two-sided 95% confidence interval of half-width 0.03. The formula n = z²·p(1−p)/ME² with z=1.96 (exact standard normal 97.5th percentile), p=0.70, and margin of error ME=0.03 yields an exact sample size of 896.37, which rounds upward to 897 participants.
assumptions: Normal approximation to binomial distribution is appropriate
Exact standard normal 97.5th percentile = 1.96 (two-sided 95% confidence interval)
Target proportion p = 0.70 used as planning proportion
Sample size rounded upward to nearest integer using ceiling function
limitations: Normal approximation assumes np and n(1−p) are both reasonably large; at n=897, p=0.70: np≈628, n(1−p)≈269, both well above conventional thresholds
Calculation assumes simple random sampling from an infinite or very large population
Actual confidence coverage may differ slightly from 95% in finite samples due to discreteness of the binomial
This is a two-sided confidence interval design; one-sided formulations would require different critical values

executions.code:
# Parameters
p <- 0.70              # Target proportion
ME <- 0.03             # Margin of error (half-width of CI)
z_alpha_2 <- 1.96      # Exact standard normal 97.5th percentile (two-sided 95% CI)

# Normal approximation formula for proportion confidence interval
# Margin of error: ME = z * sqrt(p(1-p)/n)
# Solving for n: n = z^2 * p(1-p) / ME^2

n_exact <- (z_alpha_2^2 * p * (1 - p)) / (ME^2)

# Round upward to nearest integer
n_rounded <- ceiling(n_exact)

cat("Proportion estimation sample size calculation\n")
cat("==============================================\n")
cat("Target proportion (p):", p, "\n")
cat("Margin of error (half-width):", ME, "\n")
cat("Confidence level: 95% (two-sided)\n")
cat("Standard normal critical value (z_0.025):", z_alpha_2, "\n")
cat("Variance term p(1-p):", p * (1 - p), "\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Formula: n = z^2 * p(1-p) / ME^2\n")
cat("Calculation: n = (", z_alpha_2, ")^2 * ", p, " * ", 1-p, " / (", ME, ")^2\n")
cat("             n = ", z_alpha_2^2, " * ", p * (1 - p), " / ", ME^2, "\n")
cat("             n = ", z_alpha_2^2 * p * (1 - p), " / ", ME^2, "\n")
cat("\n")
cat("Exact sample size (n):", n_exact, "\n")
cat("Rounded upward (ceiling):", n_rounded, "\n")

# Create result for structured output
result_df <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_rounded,
  unit = "participants_total"
)

library(jsonlite)
POWER_AGENT_RESULT <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_rounded, unit = "participants_total")
  )
)

cat("\n")
cat("JSON Output:\n")
cat(toJSON(POWER_AGENT_RESULT, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
